newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate finance chair lists changes to tax bill.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate finance chair lists changes to tax bill.

text.p: U.S. Senate Finance Committee Chairman William Roth said on Thursday that agreement had been reached in the panel on a tax cut bill, including changes to the initial plan.
Among the changes would be revisions to a proposal that would raise revenues from airline ticket taxes, as well as a new measure to increase the federal tax on cigarettes.
Roth said the cigarette tax proposal would raise the tax by about 20 cents per pack. The current federal tax on cigarettes is 24 cents per pack.

Roth said the initial airline ticket tax proposal to impose a 10 percent tax on the portion of an international ticket that represented flight in U.S. airspace would be scrapped. That provision would be replaced by a 10 percent tax on domestic segments of international flights and an $8 departure and arrival tax. Currently there is a $6 departure tax.
"After long discussions, many differences, agreement has basically been reached on the tax cuts," Roth, a Delaware Republican, said.
The committee reconvened an open meeting to consider the $85 billion net tax cut legislation after meeting behind closed doors for hours.
